leader_updates.round5_delta: New cell audit887 values; human isogenic precedents; PIK3C3 all-zero/finite-IC50 conflict; enzyme-concentration qualification; terminal-only PK; exact comparator47 prioritized for qualification; four independent proof-design corrections accepted.
round6_delta: New 2026 mitochondrial-fusion paper and linked 2025 thesis sharpen an on-target question; distinguish single-beta depletion, dual catalytic add-back and dual cardiomyocyte loss.
Recovered long-term kinase-dead supplement does not provide an animal denominator; separate vascular single-isoform redundancy supports a plausible, endpoint-specific window.
Adult local Mtm1 deletion and diaphragm-versus-resting-breathing comparator sharpen translational claims without adding exact-BLU efficacy.
Adult clinical cohort lineage, age/sex structure, biomarker compartment and unresolved caption arithmetic inform endpoint selection; DYN101/TAM toxicity is not assigned to BLU.
Earlier continuation evidence on VPS34, withdrawal/p62 discordance, ASPIRO lineage and ASP2957 is integrated without counting it as new round6 research.
leader_updates.round8_delta: Original precursor connectivity, enzyme-code/substrate issues, native detection route, selected force model, staged energy/safety comparison, quantitative provenance and independently reviewed decision utility.

leader_updates.name: Enasidenib for germline IDH2-R140Q D2HGA2
leader_updates.decision: Defined clinical development priority: recommend a bounded pediatric article/exposure project linked to prospective organ function.
leader_updates.exact_entity: Enasidenib; mesylate tablet reference and documented pediatric sprinkle use. Intended infant presentation must be specified; historical clinical lot identity with EP4058028B1 is unverified.
leader_updates.population: Direct human treatment anchor is germline heterozygous IDH2-R140Q. R140G, type-I D2HGDH disease and other IDH2 variants do not inherit efficacy.
leader_updates.functional_evidence: One clear severe-cardiomyopathy trajectory: LVEF 20–25% at entry, 35–40% at six months and 40–45% at eight months with later fluctuation and concurrent care. A second original child had normal baseline systolic function; Gold had milder baseline disease. Biochemical suppression is strong; neurological outcomes are less causally secure.
leader_updates.biological_units: Five outcome case records across three publications; original two and Gold are clearly distinct. Cross-publication linkage of two skin cases is unresolved. Metadata-only five-week-old report adds zero verified outcomes.
leader_updates.material_route: Defined marketed tablet and research free-base routes; actual studied sprinkle and concrete minitablet patent. Public route and historical use do not establish received lot, present supply or infant administration compatibility.
leader_updates.model_route: ATCC R140Q TF-1/parent route is biochemical, homozygous and cancer-line specific. Endogenous heterozygous mouse and genetic reversibility precedents exist. A new human cardiac model is optional when it discriminates a consequential exposure/function question.
leader_updates.exposure_and_safety: Current adult PK includes 7.9-day half-life, tenfold accumulation, 29-day steady state, active metabolite, interactions and plausible A3 antagonism. No infant dose rule or lifelong safety boundary. Direct pediatric ALT/CK observations require a coherent longitudinal exposure/laboratory timeline.
leader_updates.public_rights_and_contribution: Existing clinical program and published granted pediatric minitablet composition/process claims prevent a first-pediatric-formulation or open-rights claim. Define an improvement in delivery, exposure, burden/tolerability or prospective clinical evidence; standalone value capture remains unresolved.
leader_updates.deciding_proof: One specified pediatric administration/exposure question linked to chiral D-2-HG and a preselected organ-function outcome. Define cardiac, CNS or preventive claim; compare vorasidenib attributes for a CNS product. Clinical evidence and proprietary value remain separate.
leader_updates.advance_condition: Reliable delivery and interpretable exposure/PD plus a useful organ-function or preservation signal justify confirmation; a larger product program requires independently supported clinical benefit and a real product advantage.
leader_updates.stop_or_redirect_condition: Redirect delivery failure or exposure-related harm; narrow tissue/genotype/timing claims when appropriate. Do not reject human observations from an unqualified model. Stop a standalone product thesis if no useful incremental contribution or practicable product route exists.
leader_updates.round7_delta: Full clinical lineage and 177-cell laboratory audit; specific public pediatric formulation, adult PK/DDI/A3 and model audit; staged clinical proof with independent challenge. Removed from the reserve list to avoid conflicting current dispositions.
leader_updates.round8_delta: R140Q-active vorasidenib added as CNS mechanism/exposure comparator; tumor PK is not normal infant-brain exposure or safety superiority. Cardiac treatment, neurological benefit and neonatal prevention split. Existing sprinkle requires a demonstrated new administration/exposure contribution.

leader_updates.name: Ruxolitinib 1.5% cream for refractory Hailey–Hailey disease
leader_updates.decision: Defined controlled clinical-proof priority: recommend marketed-article, protocol and measurement qualification followed by a contemporaneously controlled patient-benefit comparison.
leader_updates.exact_entity: Prospective standardized Opzelura 1.5% cream, 15 mg/g ruxolitinib base equivalent as 19.8 mg/g phosphate. Historical cases verify active/concentration/route, not every brand, vehicle or lot.
leader_updates.functional_evidence: Five distinguishable exact-strength case reports support useful local control. Monotherapy-style treatment, add-on induction and topical maintenance are kept separate. No controlled exact-rux HHD effect estimate was verified.
leader_updates.biological_units: Five selected single-patient reports, not a consecutive treated denominator. EADV duplicate and separate 1%+naltrexone report excluded from that count. Nine-patient preprint remains abstract-only and unpooled.
leader_updates.material_route: Manufactured marketed cream defines a clinical article. Research free base/phosphate are assay routes, not equivalent clinical formulations. Qualified matched vehicle is one option; pragmatic randomized whole-product add-on comparison is a defined alternative.
leader_updates.model_route: ATP2C1 engineered/organotypic research precedents, with parent identity and assay-stage limits. Optional mechanism work only; immune-free model negativity cannot rule out an inflammatory clinical mechanism.
leader_updates.exposure_and_safety: AD PK: 479-person 1.5% phaseIII subgroup, mean Css 35.7 nM; maximum-use n=40 mean 104 nM with high-exposure extremes. No HHD PK boundary. 281 nM is a laboratory proxy, not a universal safety threshold; follow current label/combination context.
leader_updates.public_rights_and_contribution: Existing composition/formulation claims and branded franchise; current ANDA litigation. KB111 and guselkumab are active distinct HHD programs. Controlled data may be valuable, while a proprietary asset needs a differentiated benefit and executable rights/manufacturing/regulatory route.
leader_updates.deciding_proof: Controlled standardized1.5% cream plus protocolized care against the same care; preselected meaningful pain/erosion/rescue/burden outcome, masked assessment, exposure and all-randomized/maintenance denominators. Procedure avoidance requires a relevant sweat-control comparison.
leader_updates.advance_condition: Controlled useful clinical benefit or comparable efficacy with a meaningful burden/tolerability advantage, interpretable exposure and acceptable observed safety; exploratory evidence can justify independent confirmation.
leader_updates.stop_or_redirect_condition: Rule out a meaningful benefit only with an informative design and adequate delivery; redirect measurement/article failures. Stop the proposed product for reproducible unacceptable effective-exposure harm or no differentiated product contribution.
leader_updates.round7_delta: Five-report clinical audit, DERM101 concurrent-control benchmark, mechanistic citation correction, quantitative PK/high-exposure and official-patent audit, current competitors and a staged clinical proof. No new lead counted.
leader_updates.round8_delta: OnabotulinumtoxinA sweat-control benchmark added. Seven-person randomized study is separate from30-person mixed pilot with26HHD/4Darier and11HHD relapses. Late survivor efficacy is not all-randomized maintenance. Product contribution includes sustained control and lower treatment/rescue burden.

new_screens.name: Fluoxetine in KCNC1 gain-of-function disorder
new_screens.alias_audit: No prior exact KCNC1/Kv3.1/V434L/V425M use was located. Fluoxetine for slow-channel CMS was already reviewed in Round 6 and is a different exact use.
new_screens.decision: Conditional clinical-research reserve and methodological benchmark; no S-tier or precision-therapy confirmation.
new_screens.exact_article_genotype_route: The 2026 trial used oral fluoxetine powder mixed with medical corn starch in a capsule opened onto yogurt; its API salt, manufacturer and lot are not verified here. The participant carried de novo heterozygous `NM_001112741.2:c.1300G>C`, p.Val434Leu. A prior uncontrolled child had c.1273G>A, p.Val425Met. These variants and seizure phenotypes remain separate; neither supports using a Kv3.1 inhibitor in loss-of-function MEAK. [F1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13360919/) · [F2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37203213/)
new_screens.functional_evidence_and_biological_units: The 40-week trial randomized blinded transition times within a fixed placebo–fluoxetine–placebo order. One child's serial observations gave a time-adjusted primary Early Motor Questionnaire effect of **6.61 points, 95% credible interval −0.53 to 14.78**. The interval includes no treatment benefit. Purposeful hand movement and other secondary observations were suggestive; they do not multiply the participant count or rescue the primary uncertainty. NCT06341127 describes this same trial. [F1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13360919/) · [F3](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06341127)
new_screens.contrary_evidence_and_interpretation: Maturation, caregiver reporting, fixed treatment order, slow elimination and carryover complicate developmental inference. The sequential higher dose does not provide a randomized dose-response comparison. EEG excitation increased without observed clinical seizures; withdrawal-period irritability occurred. The older V425M work used transiently transfected CHO cells, not a demonstrated patient-derived neuronal model. [F1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13360919/) · [F2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37203213/)
new_screens.material_model_exposure_comparator: A described pharmacy preparation and ordinary heterologous channel assays provide routes for future independent work. Exact article/stability qualification and individual parent/metabolite exposure remain missing. A clinical dose or EEG shift cannot establish brain Kv3.1 occupancy. Mechanistic comparison should include wild-type/mutant coexpression at measured free concentrations; positive modulators for loss-of-function KCNC1 answer an opposite functional question.
new_screens.independent_challenge: A primary 2024 investigator poster reports a fluoxetine IC50 of **12.3 µM** in V434L CHO-K1 thallium-flux validation, not patch clamp or patient neurons. Its later primary investigator summary says neither fluoxetine nor norfluoxetine met the screen's 90% inhibition hit rule; this does not exclude partial modulation. The 2026 VU0521426/VU426 paper offers a state-dependent mechanistic comparator, but broad Kv-channel inhibition and low-concentration hyperpolarizing gating shifts prevent a selective-drug claim. Different assay potencies must not be converted into a clinical superiority ratio. This comparator is not a seventh screened clinical lead. [F4](https://www.metrionbiosciences.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/KCNC1_SLAS-Europe-2024_poster_final.pdf) · [F5](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00239.2026) · [F6](https://metrionbiosciences.com/hts-ion-channel-drug-repurposing-kcnc1/)
new_screens.value_capture_next_proof_advance_stop: The immediate contribution would be better variant-specific evidence, a credible exposure bridge, or a more selective article. Generic fluoxetine availability does not create exclusivity. First determine whether the claimed channel mechanism is plausible at clinical exposure; then predefine a meaningful developmental outcome, independent masked assessment, stable cointerventions and carryover handling. Reproducible useful function and tolerability advance the clinical-research case. Failure of exposure plausibility stops the *precision Kv3.1* claim even if a nonspecific symptomatic effect remains possible. Persistent trivial/null benefit stops expansion of this product thesis. No automatic treatment-withdrawal requirement is proposed.

new_screens.name: Lisdexamfetamine in KCNMA1-N999S PNKD
new_screens.alias_audit: No prior KCNMA1/lisdexamfetamine use was located. N999S and Asn1053Ser are transcript-dependent aliases, not separate candidates; Asp789Glu is a distinct genotype.
new_screens.decision: Strongest new prospective clinical-evidence question in this set; selected cases and weak exclusive-product contribution remain material.
new_screens.exact_article_genotype_route: The six-case series involved heterozygous KCNMA1-N999S; two also carried R1128W designated benign by the authors. Capsules, chewable tablets and combinations were used, so there is no single historical formulation/lot. A prospective article could specify marketed lisdexamfetamine dimesylate. N999S/Asn1053Ser is a transcript alias. A 2025 Asp789Glu case and earlier N536H/dextroamphetamine case are different genotype/article records, not additional N999S replications. [L1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8810426/) · [L2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40812354/)
new_screens.functional_evidence_and_biological_units: All six patients were **already known to the authors as responders before selection**. Retrospective parent estimates described large reductions in frequent daily episodes; three had no reported episodes during the medication-effect window. This is meaningful apparent function, but it is not a six-of-six response estimate for an unselected treated population. Reported onset/duration are caregiver observations, not measured patient PK. [L1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8810426/)
new_screens.contrary_evidence_and_interpretation: Mood/aggression, appetite and sleep effects constrained dose or coverage. Neither lisdexamfetamine nor dextroamphetamine directly altered BK-channel activity in the reported heterologous work; relief does not establish channel correction. One patient started at nine and was twenty at assessment, while others were children. The July 2026 label does not recommend use below six because of higher exposure and adverse effects; the younger published cases do not establish approval or a safe regimen for that age. [L1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8810426/) · [L3](https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=da3148af-f9b6-4725-adae-3595b4c7dc4b)
new_screens.material_model_exposure_comparator: A marketed article and prospective video-based event assessment are public routes for later regulated clinical research; a proprietary cell line is not necessary. New BK target assays would not by themselves explain an indirect stimulant effect. An exact dextroamphetamine comparator could distinguish prodrug coverage/burden if clinically appropriate; it is not assumed equivalent. A bounded ClinicalTrials.gov KCNMA1 query returned a natural-history registry and an unrelated healthy-volunteer emodepside study, not a dedicated lisdexamfetamine PNKD trial. This is not proof that no program exists anywhere.
new_screens.value_capture_next_proof_advance_stop: This is the strongest new **clinical-evidence** question in this set: prospectively enroll eligible genotype-defined patients, record nonresponders, independently adjudicate events and quantify interrupted daily activity. Separate attention/mood changes from PNKD benefit and preserve growth, appetite, sleep and cardiovascular tradeoffs. Advance if useful PNKD control generalizes beyond selected responders with acceptable burden. Stop a broad product claim if the effect is confined to selected cases, is only an attention benefit, or requires unacceptable coverage-related harms. The obvious value is evidence and a better coverage/burden solution; no exclusive asset has been identified.

new_screens.name: N-acetyl-L-leucine in GM2 gangliosidoses
new_screens.alias_audit: N-acetyl-L-leucine/Aqneursa was an NPC comparator in Round 5. GM2 is a new exact use in this corpus; GM2 gene-therapy records are different interventions.
new_screens.decision: Competitive clinical benchmark; hold new independent asset development absent a distinct contribution.
new_screens.exact_article_genotype_route: IB1001/N-acetyl-L-leucine/levacetylleucine is the single L-enantiomer, distinct from N-acetyl-DL-leucine and N-acetyl-D-leucine. The trial used oral powder suspended in ORA-Blend in genetically confirmed Tay-Sachs or Sandhoff disease, ages six to fifty-five. Individual HEXA/HEXB variants were not fully re-extracted. Current Aqneursa granules are a defined marketed article, but the formulation bridge is not proven by the common active name. [N1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9990862/) · [N3](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219132s002lbl.pdf)
new_screens.functional_evidence_and_biological_units: The open-label six-week treatment/six-week washout study used masked central video raters: **30 enrolled, 29 modified intention-to-treat, 27 washout completers**. The CI-CS contrast was 0.71 ± 2.09, with a 90% Hodges–Lehmann interval of 0–1.50. Paper p=.039 differs from the posted registry's one-sided Wilcoxon p=.044; these are one cohort, not confirmation. Registry reclassification counts **16/29 improved, 12 worsened, one unchanged** on treatment; washout counts use 27. [N1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9990862/) · [N2](https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT03759665)
new_screens.contrary_evidence_and_interpretation: No aggregate improvement was demonstrated on objective walk/peg measures or total SCAFI; only seventeen could perform the walk and twenty-three the peg task at the relevant visits. Treatment assignment lacked randomization or concurrent placebo; the paper calls the evidence Class IV. Short symptomatic change cannot establish disease modification or infantile-GM2 benefit. Five attributed adverse events occurred in three patients. [N1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9990862/)
new_screens.material_model_exposure_comparator: The marketed granule article and functional assessments supply a practical route. Neither normal infant CNS exposure nor individual GM2 target engagement was established here. Any controlled proof should prespecify ambulatory/nonambulatory strata, suitable tasks, missingness and optimized supportive care. The NPC and A-T trials are not GM2 controls, and an extension of IB1001-202 does not create a new independent cohort.
new_screens.value_capture_next_proof_advance_stop: IntraBio has the active program and branded franchise. The **September 2026 FDA label includes NPC and A-T, not GM2**; EMA's GM2 orphan designation names IntraBio and is not approval. A new independent asset thesis is therefore on hold absent a distinct contribution. Reconcile the paper/registry analysis and design controlled, clinically meaningful GM2 proof only if it fills a real gap. Benefit plus a credible product/evidence contribution could advance; another positive uncontrolled comparison alone should not. [N3](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/219132s002lbl.pdf) · [N4](https://intrabio.com/clinical-trials/) · [N5](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/orphan-designations/eu-3-17-1949)

quantitative_audit.lineage: All counts belong to IB1001-202; publication and registry are not independent cohorts.

new_screens.name: Roflumilast 0.3% cream in Darier disease
new_screens.alias_audit: Expands Round 2 proposal BL-N05, topical PDE4 inhibition after epithelial injury. The present exact use is 0.3% cream in ATP2A2/Darier disease.
new_screens.decision: Add as a concrete Darier comparator and limited clinical-research reserve; not HHD evidence or an S-tier asset.
new_screens.exact_article_genotype_route: The 2026 report concerns once-daily **0.3% topical cream**, not foam, other cream strengths or oral roflumilast. The fifteen-year-old patient had a heterozygous ATP2A2 missense variant, without the exact nucleotide/protein substitution reported. Brand and lot were not verified. Zoryve 0.3% cream is a possible specified prospective article; case evidence does not automatically establish brand identity. [R1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13586814/) · [R2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=ec1bb0d1-f38a-4080-831a-68791d1d1fdb)
new_screens.functional_evidence_and_biological_units: One patient reported marked improvement within a week and near clearance at four weeks: treated-area BSA approximately 20%→0%, itch NRS 8→0, with residual sideburn disease where application was limited. Historical corticosteroid/tacrolimus failure is not a randomized comparator. The report supplies no controlled maintenance, withdrawal, mechanical-cohesion or barrier-function result. A conference poster mentioned in its discussion was not independently verified or pooled. [R1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13586814/)
new_screens.contrary_evidence_and_interpretation: Spontaneous fluctuation, vehicle effects and a short follow-up remain alternatives. There is no Darier-specific lesional/plasma PK here. Useful anti-inflammatory symptom control is possible without demonstrating correction of SERCA2. This is **ATP2A2/Darier evidence, not ATP2C1/HHD evidence**. Add the exact cream to the NDC-9009 same-indication comparator plan; retain the distinction between clinical symptom control and delayed adhesion/barrier repair.
new_screens.material_model_exposure_comparator: A specified marketed 0.3% cream and prospective clinical lesion assessment provide a route for independent proof without an author-owned model. If the desired claim is adhesion repair, an independently qualified ATP2A2/control skin system and local exposure assessment are needed; their availability and performance are not assumed from the clinical report.
new_screens.value_capture_next_proof_advance_stop: Arcutis has a marketed topical franchise; its 2025 Form 10-K describes formulation claims and patent litigation. No freedom-to-operate conclusion follows. A controlled lesion/itch/rescue-burden study could be useful, while a separate asset needs an improved article or other concrete contribution. Skin-model repair need not be a prerequisite for clinical symptom proof, but it is necessary for a repair claim. Advance meaningful controlled function or burden benefit at tolerable exposure; stop independent product expansion if it adds no advantage over appropriate current care. [R3](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1787306/000178730626000018/arqt-20251231.htm) · [R4](https://www.arcutis.com/pipeline/)

existing_use_updates.name: W7 in TNNT2-R94C restrictive cardiomyopathy
existing_use_updates.alias_audit: The TNNT2-R94C thin-filament-desensitization use already appears as screen-index:accessible-cellular-01:511. Identifying W7 does not make it a new-use screen.
existing_use_updates.decision: Deprioritize exact W7 as a systemic article; retain selective thin-filament-desensitization discovery.
existing_use_updates.exact_article_genotype_route: W7/W-7 is N-(6-aminohexyl)-5-chloro-1-naphthalenesulfonamide. The exact salt, vendor/lot and concentration series in the 2025 R94C experiment remain unverified from the accessible text. This is an in-vitro article, not a qualified systemic formulation. One TNNT2-R94C patient-derived hiPSC background was compared with CRISPR-corrected cells. The original record already exists in the inventory. [W1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12802102/)
existing_use_updates.functional_evidence_and_biological_units: Traction force, diastolic tension, contraction/relaxation and near-simultaneous calcium signals are real functional readouts. Both W7 and mavacamten reduced diastolic dysfunction; W7 had a smaller systolic penalty, **not demonstrated absence of one**. Differentiation batches were modeled as random effects; exact well/batch counts and doses were not recoverable from the accessed figure caption. The 2016 cTnI-R193H mouse work is a different gene/allele, not a second R94C patient. [W1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12802102/) · [W2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967205/)
existing_use_updates.contrary_evidence_and_interpretation: An independent primary study found direct blockade of hERG (**IC50 3.5 µM**), Kv1.5 (6.5 µM) and Kir2.1 (13.4 µM) in HEK293 cells, separate from calmodulin inhibition. These nominal concentrations overlap the older 1–10 µM sarcomere-effect range. This is not a calculated clinical arrhythmia margin, but it is a substantive reason to deprioritize systemic W7 before assuming a usable window. Older experiments also show reduced contractility in normal myocytes. [W3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2992901/) · [W2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967205/)
existing_use_updates.material_model_exposure_comparator: Public structure and ordinary channel assays are available. Published patient-line access and detailed methods are not independently established; an engineered R94C/control pair would be a new qualification project. Compare matched useful diastolic benefit while preserving systolic reserve and electrical function, rather than comparing arbitrary equal doses. The September 2026 pediatric mavacamten approval concerns obstructive HCM, not RCM. Selective thin-filament desensitization may have a discovery/chemistry contribution; an old promiscuous probe is not already that product. [W4](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-first-drug-improve-functional-capacity-and-symptoms-children-rare-inherited-heart)
existing_use_updates.next_finite_proof_advance_stop: Restrict exact W7 to a bounded public-data/chemistry review unless a measured exposure window separates useful relaxation from electrical and systolic harm. If no such window emerges, redirect to a defined selective desensitizer. That stops the molecule thesis without disproving the target class. The independent Round 8 W7 review strengthens this disposition.

existing_use_updates.name: Epalrestat in PMM2-CDG
existing_use_updates.alias_audit: Same molecule, disease and NCT04925960 as historical-topics:T173; this is a decision-changing update.
existing_use_updates.decision: Hold independent epalrestat/PMM2 development after verified trial futility; preserve the absence of public arm results.
existing_use_updates.exact_article_genotype_route: This is the already inventoried oral epalrestat/PMM2-CDG program. NCT04925960 enrolled molecularly confirmed biallelic PMM2 cases aged two to seventeen, using oral treatment and matching placebo. Exact trial API grade/formulation and variant-specific arm results are not established by the public registry. [E1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04925960)
existing_use_updates.functional_evidence_and_biological_units: The early single-child study reported ataxia/growth improvement alongside sorbitol, transferrin and fibroblast-glycosylation changes. The later randomized trial has **42 actual participants** and official status **TERMINATED; “Due to futility.”** The early child's overlap with that cohort was not resolved, so a forty-three-person count would be unsupported. [E2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34652821/) · [E1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04925960)
existing_use_updates.contrary_evidence_and_interpretation: The API has `hasResults: false`; it supplies no arm effects or failed-endpoint attribution. In the same record, `derivedSection.miscInfoModule.submissionTracking` lists an estimated first submission date of 24 August 2026 and release/reset tracking in August/September/October. These are not posted outcome tables. A third-party tracker calling the trial “reported” cannot supply missing results or override the official futility status. No new safety or PK explanation is invented.
existing_use_updates.material_model_exposure_comparator: An existing clinical program and published fibroblast route mean the missing-article problem is not the key obstacle. The randomized placebo comparison already reached a negative program decision. Sponsor/developer interests were disclosed in the early paper. Repeating an uncontrolled biomarker experiment would not constitute a persuasive new contribution, and the PMM2 result says nothing directly about enasidenib or unrelated epalrestat indications.
existing_use_updates.next_finite_proof_advance_stop: Hold new independent epalrestat/PMM2 development. Maintain a finite public-results watch and reconcile the controlled outcomes, PK and any prespecified subgroups when actually released. Only transparent evidence supporting a specific credible explanation and differentiated next product could reopen it. Missing results are not a license to create a favorable post-hoc subgroup.

allocation.unit: planning-effort points; not dollars,success probabilities or spending

selective target discovery; exact W7 deprioritized
bounded discovery and contrary-evidence updates

round8.standalone_assets: No S-tier or financeable exclusive asset established. Scientific qualification, clinical data and proprietary value remain separate.

round9.counting_rule: Two new exact uses do not imply two new molecules. Four existing candidates were reviewed; only BLU, enasidenib and KCNMA1 receive material new primary-evidence deltas. Published experiments are historical source evidence, not experiments conducted in this sprint.

delta: Adult C2α genetic inactivation shows a stress susceptibility missed by baseline assessment; a tested isolated-cell system also failed to reproduce the organismal liability. This is not measured BLU toxicity or a partial-inhibition threshold.
C2β WT/kinase-defective add-back in a tumor model separates protein/scaffold consequences from catalytic lipid-product effects. Exact perturbations and replicate units remain distinct.

A newly retrieved primary Myology2024 abstract reports discordant myogenic, calcium, 3D morphology and RyR findings in its tested systems. Model line, genotype, maturity and functional endpoint provenance remain necessary; L463S residual function and model-specific negative sensitivity are unresolved.

Retain the affirmative bounded first-proof recommendation and 55 planning points. Additional manual interpretation requirements do not change the proposed numeric thresholds or establish a systemic therapeutic window.

A primary TGA2025 assessment adds the active vorasidenib metabolite AGI-69460 exposure issue. A late-cycle mean molar predose metabolite:parent ratio is not a normal infant-brain exposure measure or AUC ratio.

The cited assessment did not establish metabolite animal brain penetration and excluded it from the population PK model; observed adolescent representation was one patient under18. Metabolite R140Q potency and unbound normal-infant-brain exposure remain unresolved.
Retain enasidenib rank2 and15 planning points. Cardiac benefit, neurological treatment and neonatal prevention remain separate; parent-only exposure comparisons cannot establish CNS superiority.
Bounded public-source comparator review found no new verified rank-changing HHD evidence beyond the preserved dossiers. Retain rank3 and10 planning points.
Keep exact1.5% article, concurrent-care comparison, all-randomized and maintenance denominators, exposure and useful pain/erosion/rescue-burden outcomes. No new HHD efficacy observation is claimed.
